newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index snaps five-day wins on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index snaps five-day wins on profit-taking.

text.p: A reaction in Bombay blue chips triggered by local profit-taking derailed a five-day-old bull run, traders said.

But they said the easing in prices did not spell the end of the roaring Bombay rally that has bolstered the index 47 percent higher, making it the best performing emerging market in Asia till the first half of 1997.
"I am stil not convinced that the market's going to come down sharply," said Jaspreet Ahuja, head of sales at Caspian Research (India). "Even if it does it will be a correction which is good."

The Bombay index shed 27.07 points to close at a provisional 4,520.95. The index earlier charged past the 4,600 mark, hitting a 34-month high of 4,605.41 -- just shy of its all-time high of 4,643.31 set on September 12, 1994.
A Reuter poll of first half company results ending June 30, 1997 for 27 firms in the BSE index issued on Wednesday also dampened market mood, participants said.

Steel, cement and automobiles were hit hard in the earnings forecast but the poll showed overall growth. "The market took a hit after Reuters flashed the forecasts, but I think the market just needed an excuse," said a dealer at a foreign brokerage.

The net profit of cement giant Associated Cement Companies was forecast to slide 64.7 percent, to an average 194.10 million rupees in the first half of 1997/98 (April-March) from 550.50 million in the year-ago period.
ACC shares skid 108.25 rupees, or 6.5 percent, to 1,564.0.
A decision by the National Stock Exchange to postpone new account trade to Thursday came as a dampener for the market, with operators unable to build fresh positions, dealers said.
"There may be a little correction but not much. The basic direction is still positive," said Prashant Purker, head of institutional sales at Peregrine Capital India Ltd.
